content:
Let \(x\) be the number of oxen that eat as much as 3 buffaloes or 4 cows.

Convert all animals to cow-equivalents:
- 3 buffaloes = 4 cows, so 1 buffalo = \(\frac43\) cow.
- \(x\) oxen = 4 cows, so 1 ox = \(\frac4x\) cow.

Initial herd consumption per day:
\[
15\left(\frac43\right)+8\left(\frac4x\right)+24
=20+\frac{32}{x}+24
=44+\frac{32}{x}
\]
Fodder lasts 36 days, so total fodder:
\[
36\left(44+\frac{32}{x}\right)
\]

After adding 40 cows and 15 buffaloes:
\[
30\left(\frac43\right)+8\left(\frac4x\right)+64
=40+\frac{32}{x}+64
=104+\frac{32}{x}
\]
This lasts 18 days:
\[
18\left(104+\frac{32}{x}\right)
\]

Equate total fodder:
\[
36\left(44+\frac{32}{x}\right)=18\left(104+\frac{32}{x}\right)
\]
\[
2\left(44+\frac{32}{x}\right)=104+\frac{32}{x}
\]
\[
88+\frac{64}{x}=104+\frac{32}{x}
\]
\[
\frac{32}{x}=16
\]
\[
x=2
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
